# Nodes Visible When Viewing a Binary Tree From One Side

> **▶ [Solve it on TrueInterview](https://trueinterview.io/questions/binary-tree-right-side-view-2)** — free, no card: a runnable editor, the sample and hidden tests, a judged verdict, and the reference solution.

## Problem

You are handed the `root` of a binary tree. Picture yourself standing to the right of the tree and looking at it; for each level, only one node can be seen from that position. Return the values of those visible nodes, listed from the top level down to the bottom level.

## Examples

**Example 1**

```text
Input: [1,2,3,null,5,null,4]
Output: [1,3,4]
```

**Example 2**

```text
Input: [1,null,3]
Output: [1,3]
```

## Hints

<details>
<summary>Hint 1</summary>

For each level, only the rightmost node is visible, so think level by level rather than node by node.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 2</summary>

Use a level-order traversal (BFS) and keep the last node of each level, or a DFS that visits right children first and records the first node seen at each depth.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 3</summary>

Remember that a left-subtree node is visible if the right side is shorter at that depth, and handle the empty tree, aim for O(n) time.

</details>
